questions.title: Fixed-design ridge regression bias, covariance, and coefficient risk
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation based on Arthur E. Hoerl and Robert W. Kennard, Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems, Technometrics 12 (1970), 55-67, DOI 10.1080/00401706.1970.10488634. Let y=X beta+epsilon for a fixed finite real n by p design X with n>p>=1 and full column rank, E(epsilon|X)=0, and Cov(epsilon|X)=sigma^2 I_n with sigma^2>0. For lambda>=0, define beta_hat_lambda=(X^T X+lambda I_p)^{-1}X^T y. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of its conditional expectation, bias, covariance, and total coefficient mean-squared error E[||beta_hat_lambda-beta||_2^2|X]. Diagonalize X^T X to express the risk coordinate by coordinate, recover OLS at lambda=0, and show from the risk derivative at zero that some sufficiently small positive penalty strictly lowers total coefficient risk relative to OLS while introducing bias. Keep finite-sample identities distinct from Gaussian distributional statements and do not infer universal optimality of one penalty. The required model-authored artifact is est_fixed_design_ridge and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen public contract. Exploratory Python or R may check matrix identities or implementation behavior. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses independent Gaussian errors at predeclared fixed full-rank designs to compare repeated-sampling coefficient means, covariances, total coefficient risk, and a paired ridge-versus-OLS risk contrast with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

source.title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems
source.author: Arthur E. Hoerl and Robert W. Kennard

request_fields.name: design_matrix
request_fields.meaning: The fixed real n by p design matrix X, represented by observations in rows and features in columns.
request_fields.shape: rectangular n by p with n>p>=1, every entry finite, and full column rank
request_fields.indexing: outer index i is observation row i and inner index j is feature column j
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, ragged or empty rows, n<=p, and rank-deficient designs.

request_fields.name: response
request_fields.meaning: The finite observed response vector y aligned row-for-row with design_matrix.
request_fields.shape: length n with every entry finite
request_fields.indexing: entry i is the response for design row i
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries and any length different from n.

request_fields.name: penalty
request_fields.meaning: The nonnegative ridge penalty lambda applied equally to every coefficient.
request_fields.shape: finite scalar greater than or equal to zero
request_fields.units: squared design units under the stated parameterization
request_fields.indexing: one scalar for all p diagonal penalty entries
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite values and negative penalties.

response_fields.name: n_observations
response_fields.meaning: The number n of design rows and aligned responses.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be an integer strictly larger than n_features.

response_fields.name: n_features
response_fields.meaning: The number p of design columns and ridge coefficients.
response_fields.indexing: equals the common row length of design_matrix
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be a positive integer smaller than n_observations.

response_fields.name: penalty
response_fields.meaning: The exact accepted nonnegative ridge penalty lambda.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must equal the accepted request value.

response_fields.name: coefficients
response_fields.meaning: The p-vector (X^T X+lambda I_p)^{-1}X^T y in design-column order.
response_fields.shape: length p with every entry finite
response_fields.units: response units per corresponding feature unit
response_fields.indexing: entry j is the coefficient for design column j
response_fields.edge_cases: Must remain finite at lambda=0 because the admitted design is full column rank.
response_fields.normalization: No sample-size rescaling of X^T X or lambda.

response_fields.name: fitted_values
response_fields.meaning: The n-vector X beta_hat_lambda in design-row order.
response_fields.shape: length n with every entry finite
response_fields.indexing: entry i corresponds to design row i
response_fields.edge_cases: Must use the returned coefficient vector without clipping.

response_fields.name: residual_sum_squares
response_fields.meaning: The unnormalized squared Euclidean residual norm ||y-X beta_hat_lambda||_2^2.
response_fields.indexing: uses every aligned response and fitted value once
response_fields.edge_cases: Roundoff-scale negative values are not valid outputs.
response_fields.normalization: No division by n or residual degrees of freedom.

response_fields.name: effective_degrees_of_freedom
response_fields.indexing: uses the same X and lambda as coefficients
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals p at lambda=0 and is strictly below p for lambda>0.
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized trace of the ridge hat matrix.

invariants.meaning: The returned coefficients satisfy (X^T X+lambda I_p) coefficients=X^T y to numerical precision, and every derived response field uses that same vector.

Applying one common row permutation to design_matrix and response preserves coefficients, penalty, residual_sum_squares, and effective_degrees_of_freedom and applies that permutation to fitted_values.
Multiplying response by a finite scalar a multiplies coefficients and fitted_values by a, multiplies residual_sum_squares by a^2, and preserves dimensions, penalty, and effective_degrees_of_freedom.
At penalty zero, coefficients equal the ordinary full-rank least-squares solution and effective_degrees_of_freedom equals p.

empirical_claims.meaning: At each frozen fixed design, beta, sigma, and positive penalty, repeated Gaussian-error ridge coefficients have means and covariance compatible with the finite-sample conditional formulas up to declared Monte Carlo uncertainty.
At each frozen setting, repeated coefficient squared error is compatible with squared bias plus covariance trace, with Monte Carlo uncertainty reported rather than treated as proof.

For the predeclared fixed designs and coefficient vectors, a predeclared positive penalty has lower paired repeated-sampling coefficient squared error than penalty zero, with the paired Monte Carlo standard error reported.
Every confirmatory call supplies the exact frozen design, generated response, and penalty and verifies the public ridge formula and output schema before aggregating outcomes.
